# FDG9173

> DO report the number of output values successfully written by an `OperationStatus` method via an `out` parameter, declared after the out parameter that reports the number of input values that were successfully processed.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12.4 Partial Writes to Buffers and OperationStatus.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9173
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Report the number of values written by '{0}' through an out parameter declared after the one for the input

FDG9173 reports an externally visible method that returns OperationStatus and has an output buffer (a parameter named destination, or else the first one of type Span<T> or Memory<T>) when it has no out parameter of an integer type, when it has an input buffer (found as for FDG9171) and its only such out parameter ends with Consumed, or when an out parameter whose name ends with Written comes before one whose name ends with Consumed. Out parameters with other names cannot be told apart and are not reported, nor are methods that write to the state of the instance, overrides and interface implementations, so coverage is partial. Adding or moving a parameter changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Following the earlier guidance that the input buffer and output buffer should be the first and second parameters, respectively, an `OperationStatus` method should generally have a method signature like the following example to read a list of numbers:

```csharp
public static OperationStatus ReadInt32List(
  ReadOnlySpan<char> source,
  Span<int> destination,
  out int charsConsumed,
  out int valuesWritten) { ... }
```
